top.title: Joe Root to lead England in South Africa Tests; Shoaib Bashir and Ollie Pope left out
top.description: England have announced a 15-member squad for their three-match Test series against South Africa, which will be part of the 2025-27 World Test Championship (WTC). Joe Root will captain the side, while Liam Patterson-White has received his maiden Test call-up following an impressive County Championship season in 2026. Patterson-White was the most successful spinner in the competition, earning him a place in the squad. Jacob Bethell has also returned after recovering from a knee injury. However, spinner Shoaib Bashir and batter Ollie Pope have been left out. Dan Lawrence makes a comeback as an additional batting option who can also contribute with the ball. New faces and changes in England's squad England's pace attack includes Jofra Archer, Gus Atkinson, Ollie Robinson, Sam Cook and Sonny Baker. Explaining the selection, national selector Marcus North said the team was prepared for a tough challenge against the reigning World Test champions. “We have selected a strong and balanced squad that is ready for the challenge of facing a South African team that are ICC Test World Champions and who returned to the top of the ICC Test rankings following their recent 2-1 series win over Australia,” North said. He also confirmed two changes from the squad that defeated Pakistan 3-0 in the home summer series, with Patterson-White earning his first call-up and Bethell returning from injury. WTC standings and series schedule England are currently sixth in the WTC 2025-27 standings with 38.64 percentage points, while South Africa are second with 71.43 per cent. The series will begin in Johannesburg from December 17 to 21. The second Test will be played in Centurion from December 26 to 30, while the final match is scheduled in Cape Town from January 3 to 7. The tour will follow England's limited-overs series in Australia. England squad: Joe Root (c), Jofra Archer, Gus Atkinson, Sonny Baker, Jacob Bethell, Harry Brook, Sam Cook, Jordan Cox, Ben Duckett, Emilio Gay, Dan Lawrence, Liam Patterson-White, Ollie Robinson, Jamie Smith, Josh Tongue

top.description: Gary A. Vasquez-Imagn Images Oilers coach Mike Babcock explains Jake Walman scratch vs. Rangers appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Edmonton Oilers are off to a terrific start in 2026-27, winning 12 times in 18 tries and leading the Pacific Division in the early going. The same can’t be said for Jake Walman, who has managed just one assist in 11 contests, along with a minus-eight rating. He’s set to be a healthy scratch for the fifth time in the last seven games when the Oilers welcome the New York Rangers to Rogers Place on Monday night. Head coach Mike Babcock explained the decision after the team’s morning skate. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “I just think the bottom line is: what do you do without the puck? What chances are you involved in? What do you do when you have it?” Babcock told reporters, including Daily Faceoff Edmonton’s Michael Menzies. “And it’s a hard, hard league, and so each and every night, we evaluate the whole situation, and unlike you guys who watch it once, we watch it over and over again with five people, and so we got a pretty good handle on the thing. “Then, lots of times, the analytics from the outside aren’t what we have on the inside, and so what we do is we just try to make the best decisions to help the team be successful. At the same time, we’re trying to build everybody up so they can be the best version of themselves. And sometimes it’s hard when it’s not going your way.” Walman is the second-highest-paid defenseman on the Oilers and is in the first season of a seven-year contract with an average annual value of $7 million that runs through 2032-33. Emberson has managed two assists in 14 games, while Mukhamudullin has chipped in a goal over 13 contests. top.title: He replaced a Connecticut baseball legend. Then Dave Werkhoven built a legacy of his own
top.description: Former Shepaug baseball coach Dave Werkhoven, left, with longtime Spartans scorekeeper Ray Reich. (Courtesy of the Werkhoven family) WASHINGTON, Conn. - It's a truism in sports that you don't want to be the coach who replaces a legend. Yet Dave Werkhoven not only replaced the man who built the Shepaug baseball program, he became an icon in the community in his own right. And he began creating his own legacy under the most trying of circumstances. When Werkhoven had to take the helm of the Spartans late in the 1984 season, it was immediately following the death from cancer of Ted Alex, his mentor, neighbor, best friend and the man whose name already adorned the storybook ballpark in Washington Depot. "Coach Werkhoven had big shoes to fill and he more than did that," said Mike Kersten, a catcher on Werkhoven's early teams and a Shepaug assistant coach for many years. "He carried the torch of Coach Alex, and he made his own history." Werkhoven died of a stroke Tuesday, Nov. 3. He was 80. In one regard, Werkhoven even outdid Alex, winning three Class S state championships to Alex's two. Like Alex, he won more than 300 victories in his 20 years as head coach, finishing with a record of 342-103 to go with nine Berkshire League titles. "When Mr. Alex passed, it had to be a challenge to pick it up and carry it forward," said Scott Werkhoven, who succeeded his father as head coach in 2005. "But it was always about this is the way Ted did it and this is how we're going to keep doing it." A native of Ellington, Werkhoven arrived at Shepaug in 1970 with his new wife, Susan, to teach chemistry and biology. They expected to stay only a year or two, but instead spent a lifetime. Alex enlisted Werkhoven as an assistant coach at their first meeting. He also lined up the young couple with the house across the street from his, which was a strategic decision in more ways than one: The Werkhovens became convenient baby-sitters for Alex and his wife Ruth's five children. In their 15 seasons together, Shepaug won state titles in 1973 and '83. After Alex, who finished with 385 victories and 16 BL titles in 28 seasons, died on the eve of the 1984 state tournament, Werkhoven, assisted by Gerry Carbone, ran the team in the postseason. He took over as head coach the following spring. "The first three or four years, I'm sure he felt enormous pressure," said Gary Alex, Ted's son. "He would joke himself, ‘Well, I may have screwed that one up.' But you're not an assistant for 15 years without learning something." Werkhoven not only taught the same brand of baseball, but the same code of conduct. "He was an extension of Coach Alex, not only in winning, but in doing things the right way. You wear your uniform correctly; you take the field the right way. You win with humility; you lose with grace," Kersten said. "He had a quiet intensity. He would dispute a call, but he never crossed the line. I don't recall him ever swearing or using profanity." Shepaug won its first state title

top.title: Noah Gragson Owes Daniel Suarez An Apology After Homestead Spin
top.description: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images During the final laps of the NASCAR Cup Series season finale at Homestead-Miami Speedway, Noah Gragson spun Daniel Suarez. The contact happened on Lap 254 of 267 during a hard battle for 11th place. Gragson admitted he made the mistake. He did not try to hide the error or blame the track. He told the other driver he was wrong and meant it. The radio chatter before the crash made it look like the move was intentional. Gragson complained about Suarez blocking his air with 20 laps left. Insults flew over the airwaves. But the driver who caused the crash owned up to it right after the race. The two men shook hands. Gragson said the contact was not what he wanted. He just wanted to win the spot. A Full Admission of Guilt Gragson did not make excuses for hitting the left rear of Suarez’s car. He stood in front of the media and took the blame. He explained that he drove down to the bottom of the track and crossed a seam. The car got loose. He tried to save it but failed. He never wanted to spin out a competitor. The apology was clear and direct. The incident actually helped both drivers in the end. A caution flag came out after the crash. This allowed the field to bunch up. Suarez drove up to eighth place on the restart. Gragson finished ninth. They both ended up with a double top-ten finish. In the closing laps, Suarez passed Gragson without encountering any further trouble. Strong Finish for Gragson Despite the spin, Gragson finished higher than he had all season. He matched his best result of the year. Suarez secured 13th place in the final championship standings, beating absent teammate Carson Hocevar thanks to the race. Gragson felt good about the weekend despite a rough practice and qualifying session. He called Homestead one of his favorite racetracks. He noted that running the fence is fun. His car had a hole in the right-rear quarterpanel because he ran it into the wall for most of the race. “It’s probably my best racetrack and I feel like this is a place where we can at least contend and be competitive,” Gragson said, according to Motorsport.com . Grateful for a top 10 finish, he enters the offseason carrying momentum. The 2026 season ended on Sunday, November 8, 2026.

top.description: Jerod Ringwald-Imagn Images Sergio Garcia is pushing to return to the Ryder Cup after quitting LIV Golf. DP World Tour rules could prevent him from leading the squad. He has the backing of Justin Rose but needs to clear a major hurdle to get back on the team. Garcia’s departure from the rebel league puts him back in the mix for European golf, though the path is narrow. He told Golf Magic he loves the competition and wants to be part of it again. The timing of his exit aligns with a push to join the DP World Tour ahead of the next big event. A Direct Line to the Captain Garcia has already reached out to the man in charge. He confirmed a conversation with Luke Donald took place in Ireland. During that talk, Garcia said he was trying his hardest to earn a spot. Donald responded by saying he did not expect anything else from the veteran player. This exchange gives Garcia a clear sign that the captain is open to his involvement. Garcia said he told Donald directly about his effort to make the team. The captain’s reply was supportive and straightforward. Garcia told Golf Magic, “I had a little chat with Luke in Ireland, mentioning that I was trying as hard as I could to make the team, and he said that he didn’t expect anything else, so that was nice.” This support is crucial for a player trying to re-enter the fold after years away. top.title: 2026 CIAC girls soccer tournament first round is complete. What you need to know
top.description: Callie Fagan, center, of Darien fights for the ball with Grace Seltenreich, left, and Cecilia Schimenti, right, of Trumbull in Darien on October 8, 2026. (Arnold Gold/Hearst Connecticut Media) The first round of the CIAC girls soccer tournaments was held Friday and Saturday. Here is the full schedule and scoreboard for the tournaments. Here is what you need to know. Seedings hold to form The new tournament format, which factors in strength of schedule, seems to have kept seeded upsets relatively rare so far. Previously, it was just winning percentage that was used to seed the four divisions. In Class L, all 10 first-round games were won by the higher seed. In Class S, 10 of the 11 higher seeds prevailed, and the one seeded upset was a 17 beating a 16. There were three seeded upsets in Class LL: No. 21 New Canaan over No. 12 Conard, No. 19 South Windsor over No. 14 Darien and No. 18 Fairfield Warde over No. 15 Fairfield Ludlowe. Seven of the nine higher-seeded teams in Class M advanced. No. 18 Plainville eliminated No. 15 Woodland and No. 17 Lakeview beat No. 16 Nonnewaug. This system is designed to reward teams for playing a difficult schedule. For example, Darien came in with a 7-8-1 record, but had the No. 14 seed in LL, instead of being 23rd. In the end, the Blue Wave were one of the seeded upsets in the first round. Lacrosse went to a similar power points system a few years back, with the better teams getting lower-numbered seeds and two of the top three or four seeds having a better opportunity to reach the state final. You can dominate a game in soccer, run into a hot goalkeeper and lose 1-0. So we shall see how many higher-seeded teams reach the semifinals. Goalkeeper sportsmanship A number of CIAC tournament games will be decided by penalty kicks. Maybe even in the state finals. The battle for Fairfield supremacy came down to penalty kicks on Friday between Ludlowe and Warde. The two goalkeepers, Warde's Cece Meyers, a senior, and Ludlowe's Jules Conrad, a junior, were able to get through both regulation and overtime without allowing a goal. Warde coach Kim Rasmussen noted the sportsmanship between the two goalkeepers - both of whom she coached at the youth level - through the PK session. "After making big saves, the two goalkeepers exchanged high fives, celebrating and acknowledging each other's efforts," Rasmussen said in an email. "Even after Jules stepped up to take a penalty kick herself and scored against Cece, the two exchanged another high five. In a moment when the pressure was at its highest, and one team's season was about to end, these two athletes showed everyone what high school sports should truly be about." It was Fairfield Warde, the No. 18 seed, that prevailed (4-3 in PKs). The Mustangs travel to Ridgefield on Tuesday to face the second-seeded Tigers at 2:30 p.m. in an All-FCIAC matchup. Other teams may improve and put together winning runs, but Arteta’s side have already demonstrated that they can collect points regularly under different circumstances. However, their current performances provide a strong foundation from which to approach the rest of the campaign. top.title: Kansas suffers critical injury ahead of Kentucky matchup in Champions Classic
top.description: Kentucky Basketball has been battling the injury bug since back in the summer practice season. Thankfully, the Wildcats are getting healthy as regular-season play heats up, especially with Kam Williams making his return last week. The same cannot be said for the Kansas Jayhawks , who Kentucky will face in Tuesday’s Championship Classic without one of their most important players. On Monday, Kansas announced that sixth-year senior Melvin Council Jr. suffered a broken foot and will be out indefinitely. The school is hopeful that the 6-foot-4, 180-pound Council will return around the start of conference play, but for now, the standout guard will be out for the foreseeable future. That’s a massive loss for the Jayhawks, as Council is the team’s top point guard and easily one of their best players. Last season, he averaged 12.7 points, 5.1 assists, 5.0 rebounds, and 1.0 steals per game. Through two games this year, he’s averaged 8.0 points, 5.0 assists, 3.5 rebounds, and 2.5 steals in 21 minutes per game. The class of 2021 high school prospect is currently eligible thanks to a court injunction. Without Council, Kansas will rely on true freshman Taylor Kinney, a native of Kentucky, and sophomore Leroy Blyden, a transfer from Toledo who Kentucky showed interest in this past offseason . Council infamously said he was considering Kentucky prior to making his commitment on October 4. As it turned out, Kentucky, nor anyone on Council’s list, was even recruiting him, as his return to Kansas had already been a done deal, and he was simply trolling other schools.

nigeria.description: The 4-4 draw against Aston Villa felt like a victory at Old Trafford, but the fact that supporters could celebrate a point while their club sits in the relegation zone tells a more troubling story about how far United’s expectations have fallen. There was a time when a draw at Old Trafford felt like a defeat. Manchester United were a club built around winning, where anything short of three points could leave supporters disappointed, regardless of the performance. The expectation was not simply to compete but to dominate, to set the standards and to make winning feel like an obligation. Those expectations seem increasingly distant. On Sunday, Manchester United celebrated a 4-4 draw against Aston Villa with the sort of emotion usually reserved for a significant victory. Two goals in stoppage time, courtesy of Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu, rescued a point after Michael Carrick’s side had twice fallen two goals behind. The comeback was extraordinary, the atmosphere was electric and the players had every reason to appreciate their resilience. But perhaps the most revealing aspect of the afternoon was not the comeback itself. It was how much it meant. Manchester United are now in a position where avoiding defeat feels like an achievement. A point against Aston Villa, under ordinary circumstances, would hardly have been considered a successful afternoon for a club of United’s stature. Yet the circumstances have become so desperate that the draw felt like a victory. That is how quickly footballing standards can collapse. United sit 18th in the Premier League with eight points from 10 matches . They have managed just one league victory, recorded against Ipswich Town in August, and Sunday’s result extended their winless league run to eight matches. It is a club-record sequence in the Premier League. The numbers are alarming, but the deeper concern is what they reveal about the club’s changing relationship with success. Manchester United have become a team defined by what they are trying to avoid rather than what they are trying to achieve. nigeria.title: Public Notice To Gaming Operators And The General Public.
nigeria.description: FEDERAL CAPITAL TERRITORY LOTTERY REGULATORY OFFICE (FCT-LRO) O ﬃ ce of the Director-General PUBLIC NOTICE TO GAMING OPERATORS AND THE GENERAL PUBLIC. FCT-LRO COMMENCES FULL BUSINESS OPERATIONS The Federal Capital Territory Lottery Regulatory Oﬃce (FCT-LRO) hereby informs gaming operators, industry stakeholders and the general public that the Oﬃce has commenced operations as the regulatory authority responsible for the oversight, regulation and supervision of gaming activities within the Federal Capital Territory (FCT). 1. REGULATORY JURISDICTION Following the Supreme Court judgment in Attorney-General of Lagos State & 21 Others v. Attorney-General of the Federation & 15 Others, Suit No. SC/1/2008, the constitutional position on the regulation of lotteries and gaming has been clarified. By virtue of Section 299 of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria 1999 (as amended), the FCT has a distinct constitutional status, with the National Assembly exercising legislative powers ordinarily vested in a State House of Assembly. Accordingly, gaming operators conducting business within the FCT are required to comply with the applicable FCT licensing and regulatory requirements and engage with the FCT- LRO on all regulatory matters. 2. ONLINE GAMING OPERATIONS The Oﬃce clarifies that the Supreme Court judgment did not expressly settle the full regulatory framework applicable to online gaming. In particular, the judgment did not establish that any one State has exclusive regulatory control over the online gaming market. Accordingly, the online gaming market remains open to operators and investors. Operators are free to choose the regulator from whom they wish to obtain their gaming licence or authorisation, based on their business model, operational needs and the regulatory framework they consider most suitable and beneficial to their business. This choice may be exercised without undue interference, intimidation or coercive treatment by any State regulator solely on the basis that an operator has elected to obtain its licence from another regulator, as every state is duly empowered to regulate gaming activities within its relevant jurisdiction. nigeria.title: UK man convicted of fraud for secretly working five government jobs at once
nigeria.description: A 56-year-old civil servant in the United Kingdom, UK, Kashim Chowdhury has been convicted of nine counts of fraud after secretly holding multiple full-time government jobs and fraudulently earning more than £284,000 in taxpayers’ money. Chowdhury, from east London, held five overlapping government positions in the spring of 2023, concealing his multiple employment arrangements from the departments that hired him. After seven hours of deliberation, a jury unanimously found him guilty of eight counts of fraud by false representation and one count of fraud by failure to disclose. The prosecution accused Chowdhury of “deliberate, intentional dishonesty” and “exploiting the system” to secure multiple salaries from public sector employers. During the proceedings, the judge said Chowdhury faced a “very significant custodial sentence”. He also refused him bail, citing the seriousness of the offences and Chowdhury’s own wellbeing. Sarah Melo, a specialist prosecutor at the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) Serious Economic Organised Crime and International Directorate, described his actions as sustained dishonesty. “This was sustained and deliberate dishonesty,” Melo said. “He knew he could not legitimately hold multiple full-time positions at the same time, but continued to conceal what he was doing.” A spokesperson for the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Defra) said Chowdhury had “abused the trust placed in him as a public servant”. The department added that it would use all available avenues to recover the proceeds of his offending. Between 2020 and 2023, Chowdhury held eight overlapping full-time public sector positions and earned a total of £350,000, according to evidence presented in court. Prosecutors told the court that he provided inaccurate information about his employment status on job application forms and failed to disclose to government departments that he was already employed as a civil servant. After securing the positions, he also failed to inform his employers that he was working for other government departments. Chowdhury was permitted to work entirely from home after telling his employers he was caring for his mother, with whom he lived in east London. His mother had dementia and was diagnosed with terminal cancer in 2023. However, rather than reduce his workload to care for her, he continued taking on additional government positions. In the spring of 2023, he held positions across the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs, the Department of Health and Social Care, the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA), the Department for Business and Trade, the Food Standards Agency and the Home Office. During the period, he was contracted to work 183 hours a week, exceeding the total number of hours available in seven days. nigeria.title: Full list: Canada lists foreigners eligible for rural permanent residence
nigeria.description: Canada has outlined six eligibility requirements for foreign nationals seeking permanent residence through its Rural Community Immigration Program, a pathway designed to attract skilled immigrants to participating rural communities across the country. The programme offers permanent residence to eligible foreigners who want to work and settle in selected Canadian communities, particularly areas seeking skilled migrants to fill positions that cannot be filled by local residents. According to Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC), participating communities will approve designated employers to recruit skilled foreign nationals for available positions. To qualify for permanent residence under the programme, applicants must obtain a valid recommendation certificate from a participating community and secure a valid job offer from a designated employer within that community. They must also have at least one year, equivalent to 1,560 hours, of related work experience within the previous three years. Other requirements include demonstrating language proficiency through an approved test, possessing a Canadian educational credential or its foreign equivalent, and providing proof of sufficient funds to support themselves and their families. Full list of eligibility requirements According to IRCC, foreigners seeking permanent residence through the programme must meet the following six requirements: Community recommendation: Obtain a valid recommendation certificate from a participating community in Canada. Valid job offer: Secure a valid job offer from a designated employer within the participating community. Work experience: Have at least one year (1,560 hours) of related work experience within the past three years. Language proficiency: Demonstrate English or French language ability by taking an approved language test. Educational qualification: Possess a Canadian educational credential or a foreign equivalent. Proof of funds: Provide evidence of having sufficient money to support themselves and their families after arriving in Canada. The programme is designed to help participating rural communities attract skilled foreign nationals while providing immigrants with an opportunity to obtain permanent residence and establish themselves in Canada. Applicants are required to satisfy the eligibility conditions and secure the necessary community recommendation and employment offer before applying for permanent residence. nigeria.title: Court dismisses Maihaja’s suit against Wali’s APC ticket
nigeria.description: By Maryam Abdul-aziz Usman, Damaturu A Federal High Court sitting in Damaturu, Yobe State, has dismissed a suit challenging the emergence of Alhaji Baba Malam Wali as the All Progressives Congress (APC) governorship candidate for the 2027 general election. The suit was instituted by Engr. Mustapha Yunusa Maihaja, an aspirant in the party’s May 21 governorship primary, who alleged irregularities and non-compliance with the APC’s electoral guidelines. In a judgment delivered on Monday, November 9, 2026, Justice Fatima Murtala Amin held that the suit was statute-barred, having been filed outside the legally prescribed timeframe. The court also found that Maihaja failed to establish his allegations, particularly the claim of over-voting during the governorship primary. Justice Amin upheld a preliminary objection challenging the competence of the suit, thereby dismissing the case on procedural grounds. On the substantive issues, the judge identified material contradictions and inconsistencies in the testimonies of the plaintiff’s witnesses, describing the evidence as unreliable and insufficient to support the allegations. The court further held that even if the suit had been filed within the prescribed timeframe, it would still have failed on its merits because the plaintiff did not provide credible evidence to establish the alleged over-voting. Wali emerged winner of the APC governorship primary with 236,711 votes, securing the party’s ticket for the 2027 governorship election in the state. Reacting to the judgment, Wali’s Press Secretary, Shuaibu Abdullahi, commended the court for its consideration of the issues raised in the suit. “We commend the Court for its painstaking consideration of the issues and reaffirm our confidence in the judiciary as the ultimate guardian of justice and the rule of law,” Abdullahi said. The judgment dismisses the legal challenge to Wali’s emergence as the APC governorship candidate, leaving his party ticket intact ahead of the 2027 general election. nigeria.title: Barcelona teenager Pau Cubarsí wins 2026 Golden Boy Award
nigeria.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Barcelona centre-back Pau Cubarsí has won the 2026 Golden Boy award, becoming the first defender since Matthijs de Ligt in 2018 to receive the honour. The 19-year-old was recognised after a standout year with Barcelona and Spain. He helped Barça win a second consecutive LaLiga title and was part of Spain’s World Cup-winning team in North America, where he was named Young Player of the Tournament. “I’m very proud to receive the award, and I thank all the people who voted for me,” Cubarsí said in a video broadcast by Tuttosport at the ceremony. “It’s been a spectacular year, and we’re going for more,” he added. Cubarsí told Reuters that defenders can struggle to attract the same attention as attacking players. “It’s harder for defenders to get recognition… we’re less in the spotlight,” he said. “Perhaps our work isn’t as visible because, at the end of the day, the forwards score lots of goals, provide assists, play a more attractive style of football, are more eye-catching.” Spain conceded only one goal in eight matches en route to winning the World Cup, and Cubarsí played a key role in the team’s defence. He becomes the fourth Barcelona player to win the men’s award in the last six years, following teammates Pedri, Gavi and Lamine Yamal. Previous winners include Lionel Messi, Kylian Mbappé and Erling Haaland. The Golden Boy award, established by Italian newspaper Tuttosport in 2003, recognises the best under-21 player in a top European division. Journalists vote from a shortlist of nominees. About 117,000 NEAR, or roughly $430,000, passed through the six tokens, Elliptic wrote . The trail sits inside the broader laundering of the Oct. 29 Binance theft, which the exchange has put at $6.34 billion and which the FBI has attributed to North Korea’s TraderTraitor group. At no point do the stolen funds transfer directly from a buying wallet to a collecting wallet, because the pool sits in between. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine BlackRock: Security Fears Are Driving Bitcoin Whales Into IBIT Large bitcoin holders are swapping coins they guard themselves for shares of BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) at a record pace, the firm’s head of digital assets said Monday, as kidnappings and hacks push security to the top of their list. “The current moment is the highest we’ve seen at any point,” Robbie Mitchnick told Barron’s , adding that demand for the swaps “has sort of been one way — up.” Of all the reasons clients give, he said, “the single largest one is security and peace of mind.” The trades are in-kind conversions. A holder delivers bitcoin to the fund through an intermediary and receives newly created IBIT shares, without first selling the coins for cash. BlackRock relies on Galaxy Digital, Talos and Virtu to handle the transactions, and those firms set the minimum size. Barron’s put the volume BlackRock has seen at $3.6 billion, noting the real figure could be larger because the firm does not process every conversion itself. Mitchnick cited a bigger number in August, telling Bloomberg that IBIT had facilitated more than $5 billion of such swaps, up from more than $3 billion in October 2025 . entertainment.title: Nkanyeziyethu Malunga: The Zimbabwean Designer Preserving African Heritage Through Fashion
entertainment.description: At her workshop in Bulawayo, Zimbabwe, Nkanyeziyethu Malunga crafted colour into fabric, using plants, tree bark and other natural materials gathered from the environment. Choosing a colour or designing a pattern is only one of the processes. Each material carries details on how it was gathered, prepared, and transformed, which Malunga is incorporating into contemporary fashion. “My dyes are mainly extracted from plants such as mnyii and hibiscus. Although I also use many other plants, including tubers, that have properties suitable for dye extraction. I love hibiscus not only for its petals, which produce beautiful dyes, but also for its tea.” The 37-year-old designer is challenging conventional notions about what defines a fashion collection and where creative knowledge originates. Through her clothing business, GANU, she transforms indigenous materials and skills into clothes and accessories, demonstrating how knowledge passed down through generations can inform modern design, provide opportunities for rural women, and conserve cultural practices. Her method is based on teachings learned from her late maternal grandmother, Ngatsha Nkatha, who resided in Tsholotsho, a rural district in Zimbabwe. During the school vacations, Malunga and her siblings traveled from Bulawayo to visit grandma, witnessing as she turned sisal, sedge, and reeds into winnowing baskets. “When I was a child, I often visited my grandmother in the village with my siblings. She was very dexterous with her fingers, and that passion eventually became mutual.” Malunga started experimenting with fashion in her teens before launching Ganu in 2013. The name is derived from iganu, the Ndebele term for marula fruit, and represents her connection to local resources and African identity. Her creations blend basketry, crocheting, batik, and beadwork with natural dyes, leather, and other locally produced materials. For Malunga, the importance of these materials goes beyond their appearance. Bamboo, sisal, reeds, and sedge are used in basketry, and she breeds Angora goats for their fur, which she straightens and dyes to make garments. Cowhide obtained from local abattoirs is softened in a tannery before being mixed into leather designs. “I keep Angora goats for the fur needed in garment production. However, for raw materials such as cowhide, I usually source these from local abattoirs while sisal and tree barks are either harvested by me or sometimes extracted by colleagues I work with, who are based in the rural areas.” Desmond Ntini , a cultural entrepreneur based in Bulawayo, sees Malunga’s work as part of a broader shift in how African history is perceived and used. ” Malunga is redefining the fashion industry by blending traditional African influences with contemporary creativity. Somewhere between then and now, I stopped seeing real estate as a business of land and buildings. I started seeing it as a mirror. Put a property in front of a Nigerian, and you will learn, very quickly, how they think about money. Here is some of what that mirror has shown me: A prospect once told me, with complete confidence, “I have my money ready for the land.” We fixed an inspection. We walked the site together under the afternoon sun, red earth on our shoes. Then, standing on the plot, the prospect asked if they could pay next year. I was not angry. I understood. Saying “I am ready” feels good. Being ready is different. It means you have decided what the money is for, and you are willing to let it go. I have seen versions of that moment many times. The client who books an inspection for 2 pm and is still not there at 4 pm. The person who asks for options, receives ten properties that match exactly what they requested, and replies, “Do you have something else?” The buyer who is ready until it is time to decide, and then needs three more months to think. The one who disappeared after asking for a price came back after the price went up, and asked for the old price. For a long time, these moments frustrated me. entertainment.description: With Earth & Sky , her Spring/Summer 2027 collection, Banke Kuku turns to nature’s most essential cycle: the sky gives rain, the rain feeds the earth, and the earth gives back. Reimagining the water cycle as a circle of life, the collection celebrates the abundance that flows from it. Earth & Sky is built around seven prints in three families. The Sky family is led by the hero print, Bougainvillea Sky, with watercolour bougainvillea, bees, butterflies and birds drifting across a turquoise ground, alongside Dove Sky and Daybreak Sky. The Earth family, Yellow Trumpet and Flower Bud, draws on flowering plants such as Costus spectabilis . This is my most personal collection.” A CYCLE OF GIVING BACK In nature, nothing is wasted, and everything returns. Earth & Sky carries that principle as its message: what we take from the earth, we must give back. That principle extends into how Banke Kuku approaches production. The brand maintains a no-waste policy, finding uses for offcuts rather than discarding them, while its seasonless approach allows pieces to remain part of the collection beyond a single season. Banke Kuku also uses digital printing, which consumes less heat and water than conventional printing methods, and continues to reduce its use of man-made fabrics in favour of more conscious material choices. entertainment.title: Inside the Story of Martell’s Afrobeats Limited Edition XO with Davido and Prince Gyasi
entertainment.description: There’s something special about a collaboration that brings together music and visual art, particularly when both creatives have spent years helping African culture reach audiences around the world. For its latest limited edition, Maison Martell has brought together Nigerian music superstar Davido and Ghanaian visual artist Prince Gyasi to create a new expression of its prestigious XO cognac , inspired by the sound, movement and global influence of Afrobeats. The Martell Afrobeats Limited Edition XO will be unveiled in Nigeria on November 6, following the collection’s global launch in New York on October 28. At the heart of the collaboration is Prince Gyasi’s distinctive artistic language. Known for his vibrant colours and imaginative compositions, Gyasi has created an original artwork of Davido that features on the limited-edition bottle and presentation box. The design draws inspiration from the landscapes of West Africa, bringing together Martell’s iconic blue with shades of amber and gold. The blue reflects the rhythmic flow of the ocean, while the golden tones evoke sunlit sands and the warmth of African sunsets. entertainment.title: UK-based OBIMI Brings Families Together in Lagos to Support Children With Disabilities
entertainment.description: OBIMI CIC is a UK-based community organisation supporting parents and caregivers of children with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND). Its founder, Helen Ewumi , is a qualified social worker and a parent of children with disabilities. Her professional experience and family life both inform OBIMI’s commitment to helping families feel heard, supported and less alone. The Nigeria outreach brought families together in Lagos to share experiences and raise awareness about the importance of understanding disability and challenging stigma. Around 100 families received support through the outreach, including food hampers. Clothing was also shared with families. During the visit, the OBIMI team went to a special school in Lagos and gave pupils school bags and stationery. These practical gifts were offered to support children with their learning and to remind them that they are valued and included. The gathering also created space for families to connect and take part in conversations about disability. OBIMI’s message was clear: every child deserves to belong, and families should be met with understanding, respect and support. For Helen, taking OBIMI’s work to Nigeria was an opportunity to connect with families and communities in Lagos. As a social worker and a parent with lived experience of caring for children with disabilities, she understands how important it is for families to feel listened to and supported. OBIMI CIC is grateful to the families, school staff, volunteers, partners and supporters who helped make the outreach possible. The organisation hopes to continue building connections and raising awareness so that children with disabilities and their families can feel seen, supported and included. sports.title: He replaced a Connecticut baseball legend. Then Dave Werkhoven built a legacy of his own
sports.description: Former Shepaug baseball coach Dave Werkhoven, left, with longtime Spartans scorekeeper Ray Reich. (Courtesy of the Werkhoven family) WASHINGTON, Conn. - It's a truism in sports that you don't want to be the coach who replaces a legend. Yet Dave Werkhoven not only replaced the man who built the Shepaug baseball program, he became an icon in the community in his own right. And he began creating his own legacy under the most trying of circumstances. When Werkhoven had to take the helm of the Spartans late in the 1984 season, it was immediately following the death from cancer of Ted Alex, his mentor, neighbor, best friend and the man whose name already adorned the storybook ballpark in Washington Depot. "Coach Werkhoven had big shoes to fill and he more than did that," said Mike Kersten, a catcher on Werkhoven's early teams and a Shepaug assistant coach for many years. "He carried the torch of Coach Alex, and he made his own history." Werkhoven died of a stroke Tuesday, Nov. 3. He was 80. In one regard, Werkhoven even outdid Alex, winning three Class S state championships to Alex's two. Like Alex, he won more than 300 victories in his 20 years as head coach, finishing with a record of 342-103 to go with nine Berkshire League titles. "When Mr. Alex passed, it had to be a challenge to pick it up and carry it forward," said Scott Werkhoven, who succeeded his father as head coach in 2005. "But it was always about this is the way Ted did it and this is how we're going to keep doing it." A native of Ellington, Werkhoven arrived at Shepaug in 1970 with his new wife, Susan, to teach chemistry and biology. They expected to stay only a year or two, but instead spent a lifetime. Alex enlisted Werkhoven as an assistant coach at their first meeting. He also lined up the young couple with the house across the street from his, which was a strategic decision in more ways than one: The Werkhovens became convenient baby-sitters for Alex and his wife Ruth's five children. In their 15 seasons together, Shepaug won state titles in 1973 and '83. After Alex, who finished with 385 victories and 16 BL titles in 28 seasons, died on the eve of the 1984 state tournament, Werkhoven, assisted by Gerry Carbone, ran the team in the postseason. He took over as head coach the following spring. "The first three or four years, I'm sure he felt enormous pressure," said Gary Alex, Ted's son. "He would joke himself, ‘Well, I may have screwed that one up.' But you're not an assistant for 15 years without learning something." Werkhoven not only taught the same brand of baseball, but the same code of conduct. "He was an extension of Coach Alex, not only in winning, but in doing things the right way. You wear your uniform correctly; you take the field the right way. You win with humility; you lose with grace," Kersten said. "He had a quiet intensity. He would dispute a call, but he never crossed the line. I don't recall him ever swearing or using profanity." Shepaug won its first state title

sports.title: 2026 CIAC girls soccer tournament first round is complete. What you need to know
sports.description: Callie Fagan, center, of Darien fights for the ball with Grace Seltenreich, left, and Cecilia Schimenti, right, of Trumbull in Darien on October 8, 2026. (Arnold Gold/Hearst Connecticut Media) The first round of the CIAC girls soccer tournaments was held Friday and Saturday. Here is the full schedule and scoreboard for the tournaments. Here is what you need to know. Seedings hold to form The new tournament format, which factors in strength of schedule, seems to have kept seeded upsets relatively rare so far. Previously, it was just winning percentage that was used to seed the four divisions. In Class L, all 10 first-round games were won by the higher seed. In Class S, 10 of the 11 higher seeds prevailed, and the one seeded upset was a 17 beating a 16. There were three seeded upsets in Class LL: No. 21 New Canaan over No. 12 Conard, No. 19 South Windsor over No. 14 Darien and No. 18 Fairfield Warde over No. 15 Fairfield Ludlowe. Seven of the nine higher-seeded teams in Class M advanced. No. 18 Plainville eliminated No. 15 Woodland and No. 17 Lakeview beat No. 16 Nonnewaug. This system is designed to reward teams for playing a difficult schedule. For example, Darien came in with a 7-8-1 record, but had the No. 14 seed in LL, instead of being 23rd. In the end, the Blue Wave were one of the seeded upsets in the first round. Lacrosse went to a similar power points system a few years back, with the better teams getting lower-numbered seeds and two of the top three or four seeds having a better opportunity to reach the state final. You can dominate a game in soccer, run into a hot goalkeeper and lose 1-0. So we shall see how many higher-seeded teams reach the semifinals. Goalkeeper sportsmanship A number of CIAC tournament games will be decided by penalty kicks. Maybe even in the state finals. The battle for Fairfield supremacy came down to penalty kicks on Friday between Ludlowe and Warde. The two goalkeepers, Warde's Cece Meyers, a senior, and Ludlowe's Jules Conrad, a junior, were able to get through both regulation and overtime without allowing a goal. Warde coach Kim Rasmussen noted the sportsmanship between the two goalkeepers - both of whom she coached at the youth level - through the PK session. "After making big saves, the two goalkeepers exchanged high fives, celebrating and acknowledging each other's efforts," Rasmussen said in an email. "Even after Jules stepped up to take a penalty kick herself and scored against Cece, the two exchanged another high five. It was Fairfield Warde, the No. 18 seed, that prevailed (4-3 in PKs). The Mustangs travel to Ridgefield on Tuesday to face the second-seeded Tigers at 2:30 p.m. in an All-FCIAC matchup. sports.title: Kansas suffers critical injury ahead of Kentucky matchup in Champions Classic
sports.description: Kentucky Basketball has been battling the injury bug since back in the summer practice season. Thankfully, the Wildcats are getting healthy as regular-season play heats up, especially with Kam Williams making his return last week. The same cannot be said for the Kansas Jayhawks , who Kentucky will face in Tuesday’s Championship Classic without one of their most important players. On Monday, Kansas announced that sixth-year senior Melvin Council Jr. suffered a broken foot and will be out indefinitely. The school is hopeful that the 6-foot-4, 180-pound Council will return around the start of conference play, but for now, the standout guard will be out for the foreseeable future. That’s a massive loss for the Jayhawks, as Council is the team’s top point guard and easily one of their best players. Last season, he averaged 12.7 points, 5.1 assists, 5.0 rebounds, and 1.0 steals per game. Through two games this year, he’s averaged 8.0 points, 5.0 assists, 3.5 rebounds, and 2.5 steals in 21 minutes per game. The class of 2021 high school prospect is currently eligible thanks to a court injunction. Without Council, Kansas will rely on true freshman Taylor Kinney, a native of Kentucky, and sophomore Leroy Blyden, a transfer from Toledo who Kentucky showed interest in this past offseason . Council infamously said he was considering Kentucky prior to making his commitment on October 4. As it turned out, Kentucky, nor anyone on Council’s list, was even recruiting him, as his return to Kansas had already been a done deal, and he was simply trolling other schools.

technology.title: Attackers backdoor trusted AWS integrations to steal secrets
technology.description: Unknown attackers used compromised identity and access management (IAM) credentials associated with Qubole's AWS account to access customer AWS environments, stealing secrets and other sensitive data from S3 buckets. Qubole is a cloud data processing platform that uses cross-account IAM roles to manage compute and access storage in customers' AWS environments without requiring customers to provide long-lived AWS access keys. The supply-chain attack abused this third-party, cross-account trust relationship. Google’s cloud-security shop Wiz declined to tell us how many organizations were affected, but called it a “broad, opportunistic supply chain campaign” that hit “multiple” customer environments. “Because many organizations left trust policies active even after deprecating the platform, the attacker was able to successfully assume integration roles, enumerate cloud resources, harvest secrets, and siphon data,” the researchers told The Register in an emailed response to questions. Neither AWS nor Qubole responded to The Register 's inquiries. Wiz, working with Google's Mandiant incident responders after AI data security company Sentra flagged suspicious activity, traced the malicious activity back to October 14, when credentials associated with Qubole's AWS account were used to call the sts:AssumeRole API to obtain temporary credentials for customer-managed integration roles. The calls originated from Qubole AWS account 805246085872 , and used IAM user ID AIDA3W7DIFLYOLTK63SFS , Wiz analysts Zack Morrow, Sean Johnstone, and Benjamin Read said in a Monday blog about the supply chain attack. “Across the affected environments, Wiz CIRT has not observed this IAM user in any activity other than that associated with this threat actor,” the trio wrote. This activity continued on October 15, and on October 18, the digital intruders began using a second IAM user from the same account. Once inside customers’ environments, the crooks began probing a ton of AWS services and stealing credentials, keys, and other secrets stored across Lambda, Secrets Manager, and SSM Parameter Store. The miscreants also used TruffleHog to test AWS credentials belonging to victim organizations, discover their Microsoft Entra ID secrets, and request OAuth tokens using Okta client credentials also uncovered while snooping around the AWS environments. Abusing the integration roles also allowed the criminals to steal data from customers’ S3 storage, although it seems they were largely opportunistic attackers, in some cases downloading entire buckets, as opposed to state-sponsored spies looking for specific data. The threat hunters haven’t attributed the supply chain attack to any particular group, and say they don’t have any insight into how the miscreants are using the stolen data. While investigating this incident, Wiz spotted a separate campaign between October 8 and October 11 that also used customer-owned AWS access keys for Qubole integrations. technology.title: Researchers pwn automakers’ Android apps to remotely unlock cars, honk horns
technology.description: Security researchers exploited flaws in Android apps to gain remote access to connected cars from two major automakers, allowing them to start engines, flash headlights, and sound horns. Shubham Shah, co-founder at Assetnote, and researcher Sam Curry worked together on the exploits earlier this year. By tinkering with the cars’ Android apps, they devised exploit paths to issue remote commands to vehicles in Australia and the US . The pair published separate blogs covering different aspects of the research; Shah said the US attack "required a lot more work" because the automaker "spent much more time securing the US, Canadian, and European OpenIDM environments." Both exploit chains centered around weaknesses in the ForgeRock identity platform relied upon by both automakers, the identities of which were kept anonymous by the researchers, who have previously highlighted flaws in the likes of Hyundai , Kia , Subaru , and many others . In the Australian version of the app, the researchers first found a vehicle identification number (VIN) using public licence plate checkers, and used those in queries to internal APIs, which provided personal information and owner email addresses. They also found hardcoded admin credentials for the ForgeRock OpenIDM that were meant for the staging environment but also worked in production. After bypassing the heavy WAF filtering by exploiting path traversal flaws, they were able to invoke the internal admin APIs and take over target accounts using only their email addresses. This let them mint authentication tokens, which they could issue to send arbitrary commands to affected vehicles through the mobile app. Issuing commands on the US version also required bypassing WAF filtering through a path traversal, though with a more involved technique: exploiting path confusion to reach the Apache Felix admin console. The researchers used factory default credentials in Felix’s OSGi Web Console to gain admin privileges. They then used Felix configuration manager to schedule a task that executed an inline Groovy script, giving them shell access to the identity servers. The researchers then queried local admin API endpoints, allowing them to view or modify user account data. From there, they logged into car owners’ accounts, and gained the ability to issue the same commands as demonstrated in the Australian version. According to Curry’s disclosure timeline, he and Shah approached the affected automakers in "early 2026," and the exploits were patched within two hours of receiving the report. Although the automakers wished to remain anonymous, it didn’t take long for some petrolheads to speculate that the partially blurred car in Shah’s demo video was a Toyota, citing the shape of the wing mirror and the unlock sound it made. Onlookers claimed that the two automakers in question were likely Toyota and its luxury brand Lexus. technology.title: Claude Code is accidentally exposing secrets all over GitHub
technology.description: Claude Code is leaking sensitive information on public GitHub instances thanks to a partial oversight in the way its settings files are handled. That's the finding of AI security researchers at Apiiro, who discovered thousands of secrets , including database passwords, API tokens, and root logins, amid Claude Code settings files embedded in GitHub repositories. The leak stems from the way Claude Code handles user approval for automated shell commands. When a user chooses the "Yes, and don't ask again" option to approve running a command, that choice gets stored as part of a rule in the local ".claude/settings.local.json" file on the user's computer. That rule is sometimes coded as a pattern, but the command itself is often written to that settings file as is, including any sensitive information that may be embedded within it. This isn't really a significant security issue if the settings file stays on the user's local machine (assuming that machine doesn't become compromised itself, of course). And Anthropic notes in its Claude Code documentation that this particular settings file gets added to the developer's global .gitignore list , which usually prevents it from being shared publicly. This partner is either a stellar-mass black hole, or the dense collapsed core of a massive star called a neutron star. This is the first X-ray detection of one of this class of erupting stars. It is also the first of these objects found with a black hole or neutron star companion. The volatile star, known as AT 2016blu, is in the spiral galaxy NGC 4559, located about 30 million light-years from Earth. Astronomers estimate the mass of this star is at least 33 times that of the Sun. “For 15 years, astronomers have been watching this star get really bright and then dim again on a regular basis,” said Mojgan Aghakhanloo of the University of Virginia in Charlottesville, who led this study. “Until we were able to get Chandra data at the right time, we couldn’t figure out what was making this happen.” The star AT 2016blu is a type of luminous blue variable, which are hot, massive stars characterized by changes in brightness. The spikes in brightness are so extreme that they resemble supernova explosions, where a massive star collapses onto itself and material then hurtles outward into space. science.title: Netflix announces 'Stranger Things' spin-off 'Other Worlds', and it's already teasing a trip to Area 51 (video)
science.description: null So, you thought "Stranger Things" was done and dusted after all that Conformity Gate nonsense? No way! Netflix's sci-fi sensation returns in the live-action prequel series "Other Worlds: A Stranger Things Adventure." Created by the Duffer Brothers and Kate Trefry, with the episodes set to be directed by Joe Wright ("Darkest Hour", "Black Mirror"), this new show isn't set in Hawkins or the electric '80s. No, this time around, the action takes place in Marion, Nevada, in 1955, and you know what else is located in Nevada, right? Area 51 . The teaser trailer certainly teases the possibility of a trip to the world's most paradoxically famous secret military base, showcasing a bike and radio resting outside of a fence with a sign that clearly says it's a restricted area (in any TV show or film, that's actually an invitation to see what's on the other side). Of course, the tease doesn't end there, as the thunder booms in the sky and there's a visual hint of a wormhole. No story details about "Other Worlds: A Stranger Things Adventure" have been released to date, but there are some clues out there for all the Internet sleuths. Trefrey wrote the Henry Creel-focused "Stranger Things: The First Shadow" play, while Matt Duffer explained to Variety how a spin-off show would tackle the rock that Henry found in the briefcase in "Stranger Things." So, yes, expect this to be a Henry-centric affair and the start of his long, hard road to hell and becoming Vecna. (Image credit: Netflix) What'll be interesting, though, is to see how the show ties into the history of Area 51. After all, it was on April 12, 1955, that CIA officer Richard Bissell discovered the site, while the "Other Worlds" trailer has the date of April 19th clearly marked onscreen, so the timelines align nicely here. "Stranger Things" has never been shy of tying itself to real-world science and historical events, so it'll be fascinating to see how the show explores Area 51 as a concept and the secrets everybody believes are hidden there. Was it really a site to test highly advanced weapons and aircraft, or was E.T. 's cousin held hostage there until he revealed Colonel Sanders' 11 herbs and spices? Who knows, with all this renewed excitement around this mysterious military facility, we might get another "Storm Area 51" event to enjoy and laugh at all over again. Regardless, more "Stranger Things" is welcome news, and since it's presumably about one of the show's best characters, Henry Creel, it only adds another layer to his already intriguing lore. If we can't have an origin story about Hopper's incredible and envious moustache, this is the next best thing. "Other Worlds: A Stranger Things Adventure" arrives on Netflix in 2028. Meteor fireballs visible in the daytime are referred to as 'bolides'. At 1:06 p.m. local time (18:06 UTC) on May 30, 2026 one such bolide was widely witnessed falling out of the sky over coastal Massachusetts, with members of the public also reporting an associated sonic boom that rumbled across the north-eastern coast of the United States. Now, a team of scientists from Europe and the United States, led by space physicist Juha Vierinen of the Arctic University of Norway in Tromsø, have patched together measurements from a meteor-observing radar network, regular weather radar, infrasound stations and camera footage to fully characterize the fall of this meteoroid and trace its orbit around the sun . Key to these observations were measurements by the Spread Spectrum Interferometric Meteor Observing Network (SIMONe) based at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology's (MIT's) Haystack Observatory. SIMONe is a project jointly developed by MIT, the Arctic University of Norway and the Leibniz Institute of Atmospheric Physics in Kühlungsborn, Germany. "We were fortunate that the event occurred within the coverage of SIMONe," Vierinen told Space.com. This is echoed by Ryan Volz, a radio scientist at Haystack Observatory who is a member of the team who studied the May 30 bolide. "We got pretty lucky to observe this one," Volz told Space.com. "A bolide like this would have to enter the atmosphere within about 62 miles (100 kilometers) of a SIMONe-like meteor radar system for the head echoes we saw to be detectable, and there are only a handful of places in the world that currently meet that criteria." A head echo is what radar sees when a meteoroid – what we call the lump of rock that becomes a meteor while it is still in space – enters Earth's atmosphere , generating a cloud of plasma around it as it superheats the atmosphere and its outer surface. "The head echoes give the best constraints on the meteoroid's trajectory," said Volz. The existence of the head echo is usually very brief, taking place at 56 miles (90 kilometers () altitude down to about 44 miles (71 kilometers) when the plasma around the meteoroid is dense enough to return a radar echo. The head echo transitions into a 'trail echo', which is produced by a streak of turbulent plasma that is left in the wake of the meteoroid after it has passed through a given part of the atmosphere. In the case of the 30 May bolide, the trail echo was detected down to an unusually low altitude of 20 miles (32 kilometers), at which point the falling rock fragmented with an explosive force equivalent to 500 tons of TNT, whereas the total impact energy of the bolide was in the region on 1.1 kilotons of TNT.
